method: Programmatic enumeration of every action event and rrweb DOM/input/scroll stream across all 101 sessions; detailed per-success timing and comparison of failure traces. No visual replay; no form values inspected or included.

observations.claim: Every recorded input starter completes all four fields and receives success; no failure session contains an input event.
observations.confidence: high for this exported cohort; not causal proof

observations.claim: The observed loss occurs before manual form interaction, not at a difficult individual field.
Successful hero CTA clicks are late, after deep page scrolling. The early-action mechanism proposed for e03 is not demonstrated.

evidence.example_scroll: Deep y6113 then y237 then y7573 immediately around CTA

observations.confidence: high for scrolling pattern; automated selector choice is an inference

observations.claim: Fixed-looking form completion/exit timing and binary input outcomes are compatible with simulator policy decisions. Human reluctance cannot be inferred directly.
observations.confidence: observed timing high; policy explanation unproven

observations.claim: Repeated top-edge HTML clicks are not a sufficient explanation for failure because every successful session also has three.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Long content or nonfunctional card affordances accumulate friction before the form-start decision.
hypotheses.support: Every successful and nearly every failed path traverses a long page before late CTA; repeated off-target interactions exist. This is indirect, not evidence of fatigue.
hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Shorten program module text while retaining every program-module/program-list node and course facts; keep e03 CTA and form fixed. Remove pointer styling only in a separate experiment.
hypotheses.prediction: More CTA sessions produce first manual/input event; input-start-to-success remains near 100%; time before CTA declines.
hypotheses.falsifier: Pre-CTA time declines but form-start fraction does not improve.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The start decision depends on visible commitment clarity near the form.
hypotheses.support: 74 of90 CTA sessions do not begin input, but no direct evidence explains the decision.
hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Test precise truthful text stating what happens after the application and show relevant course price/format near registration, without changing required fields or backend. Avoid inventing payment/refund promises.
hypotheses.prediction: CTA-to-input-start improves without changing completion behavior once input begins.
hypotheses.falsifier: No change in starters across comparable batches.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hero CTA changes the first matching simulator selector rather than enabling immediate human-like registration.
hypotheses.support: All16 successes click hero only after36.8–56.8s and deep scrolling, followed by identical y237→7573 jumps.
hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Do not claim e03 confirms early action. Compare actual CTA timing/source distributions and preserve source tags. Prefer next change inside program section rather than adding more CTA instances.
hypotheses.prediction: If a genuine early path emerges, first CTA times should occur before deep scroll; otherwise late hero clicks persist.
hypotheses.falsifier: Substantial early hero CTA traffic before program reading.

limitations: 101 page sessions versus100 simulator visits; unique visitor attribution unavailable.
No randomization: E02=10/100 versusE03=16/100 does not by itself establish causal uplift.
Snapshot/input events can identify interaction but not motivation.
All observed sessions are simulator traffic; strategies should respect supplied challenge selectors.
No site/API/tracker changes made by this reviewer.
